nodes.label: Code invariants I1–I7
nodes.rationale: Hard laws of the project: GOV supply cap fixed (I1), CREDIT burned on consumption (I2), per-round emission cap (I3), Timelock owns critical contracts (I4), votes via ERC20Votes snapshot to prevent flash-loan attacks (I5), staking minimum lock (I6), projects enter Registry only via Timelock (I7).

nodes.label: Regulatory guard (Howey test wording scan)
nodes.rationale: Public-facing text describing the DAO token as investment/shares/dividend could satisfy the SEC Howey test and classify it as a security; agents scan for these terms and recommend reframing as governance access + utility. Soft warning, never blocks — legal decision stays with the user.

nodes.label: Economic invariants IE1–IE10
nodes.rationale: Complementary economic laws defended by dao-economist: alpha < 1 permanent (IE1), floor temporary (IE2), capMax > alpha*peak (IE3), app rebate <= 1-alpha to prevent self-payment extraction (IE4), DEX TVL >= 10x daily burn volume (IE6), buyback only below fair operational price (IE7), team vesting with cliff (IE8), no entity >= 20% distribution (IE9), no emergency pause on CREDIT/Staking (IE10).

nodes.label: REMODEL 2026-07-08 — payment rail + rev-share
nodes.rationale: The burn-to-mint model imposed an effective ~80% fee on app revenue, making bypass (direct CREDIT.transfer) the dominant strategy (Nash equilibrium = collapse). Replaced by a competitive 2.5% payment rail (FeeRouterV2), CREDIT as 1:1 USDC stablecoin (CreditPSM), and investor income from real app revenue (ProjectFunding) instead of emission; GOV captures value via fee-funded buyback.

nodes.label: Burn-to-mint economic model (legacy)
nodes.rationale: Legacy engine: users pay CREDIT via FeeRouter (split 70/20/10 burn/treasury/rebate), BurnTracker records burn per (round, projectId), next round emits min(max(alpha*burn, floor), capMax) split across buckets. alpha=0.95 guarantees mild deflation; floor decay (rounds 0-23), sanity cap and probation penalty are the three safeguards. Superseded by the 2026-07-08 remodel, kept as historical reference (README §1–§6).

nodes.label: Supermajority 75% for removePOL / role-management proposals
nodes.rationale: POL exit policy (docs/governance/fase1-2-pol.md) was only a social norm; now enforced on-chain. Because '>25% of POL' is not measurable at propose time, ANY proposal containing Treasury.removePOL is marked Supermajority (For >= 3x Against). Adversarial review added anti-bypass: grantRole/revokeRole/renounceRole targeting Treasury or the Timelock itself also trigger supermajority, otherwise a simple-majority proposal could hand out GOVERNANCE_ROLE and call removePOL directly.

nodes.label: On-chain segregation of reserved CREDIT balances
nodes.rationale: Invariants that were only comments became enforced: LiquidityGauge ledger totalVestingLocked prevents governanceRescueRewards from draining vesting-reserved CREDIT; Treasury _enforceUnreservedCredit blocks generic CREDIT outflows from invading polRefillBucket + pendingGaugeRewards; deposit side also enforced (DepositExceedsCreditBalance) to prevent ledger inflation DoS; write-down valves escape gauge freeze and recycle the bonders bucket.
nodes.norm_label: on-chain segregation of reserved credit balances

nodes.label: FFP — Floating with Floor Price
nodes.author: dao-economist
nodes.rationale: Hard peg rejected (MiCA EMT/GENIUS Act regulatory death, requires 1:1 audited reserves + licensed issuer, incompatible with permissionless DAO); soft peg rejected (still stablecoin scope + 24/7 defense overhead); pure floating rejected (apps pricing in CREDIT see 50%+ weekly cost swings). FFP: CREDIT floats freely upward, Treasury defends floor = max(0.5 x MA90, $0.10) via buyback-and-burn when spot < floor for 24h (TWAP 30min), budget caps 20%/event and 30%/month. Not legally a peg — analogous to discretionary share buyback. Death spiral eliminated because collateral is external USDC, not reflexive.

nodes.label: CLP pivot (Credit Liquidity Protocol)
nodes.author: dao-economist
nodes.rationale: Pivot from retrospective burn-to-mint DAO to Curve-style liquidity protocol approved only in 2 phases with a HARD GATE: Phase 1 (FFP buyback + POL + LiquidityGauge + bucket-aware RewardDistributorV2) uses extensions of the current stack; Phase 2 (GaugeController, VotingEscrow, BondDepository) only after 60 rounds (~15 months) of real mainnet data. Motive: Wonderland/Olympus/Iron Finance died from launching bonding + ve + gauge simultaneously without real demand data. Red flags: GOV cap vs 4y escrow decay kills governance; gauge (prospective/political) vs burn (objective usage) dissonance; C4 Treasury recurring-revenue gap must be fixed first (split 70/20/10).

nodes.label: POL — Protocol Owned Liquidity (operational params)
nodes.author: dao-economist
nodes.rationale: POL is a liquidity anchor, not a yield vehicle: without pool depth, executeBuyback swaps against an empty book and slippage devours the FFP defense. Decisions frozen: full range (concentrated ranges go one-sided exactly during crashes — anti-correlated with FFP, as Wonderland showed), fee tier 0.30% aligned with Treasury.swapFeeTier, fees claimed to Treasury without auto-compound, exit >25% requires 75% supermajority, soft cap 50% of pool. Seed size left pending user decision (Treasury has no USDC bootstrap).

nodes.label: FeeRouter bypass incentive (dominant strategy)
nodes.author: dao-economist
nodes.rationale: Routing via FeeRouter.pay returns the app owner only ~20% (no self-stake) to ~57% (100% self-stake) of each payment vs 100% via direct CREDIT.transfer, with no on-chain enforcement or punishment. Effective fee ~80% is uncompetitive even vs app stores (15-30%). Free-riders earn 5x more than honest routers while capturing the deflation others finance — prisoner's dilemma with equilibrium at collapse (burn -> 0, emission -> floor -> 0). Levers: registry collateral with teeth, setProjectSplit as commercial instrument, invert fee onto the user (network-fee model), on-chain product gating.

nodes.label: Triage ACCEPTED: TeamVesting timestamp dependence
nodes.rationale: A vesting contract is intrinsically time-dependent: the cliff/linear schedule is defined in seconds. The ~15s validator timestamp manipulation window in PoS is irrelevant at the scale of a multi-year schedule (12m cliff, 48m duration). No economic vector exploits this drift.

nodes.label: Triage ACCEPTED: TeamVesting.release amount == 0 strict equality
nodes.rationale: amount == 0 compares the return of releasable() (pure uint256, no external-token dependency). It is the canonical guard for 'nothing to release' — no rounding or adversarial manipulation makes this equality dangerous. Same pattern as Treasury.transfer's amount == 0, also accepted in triage.

nodes.label: Triage ACCEPTED: UserSubsidy campaign deadline timestamp dependence

nodes.label: Three-layer DAO architecture (political / state / economic)
nodes.rationale: Political layer (Governor + Timelock) decides what changes; state layer (Registry + Treasury + Staking + ProjectFunding) holds who and what; economic layer (CreditPSM + FeeRouterV2 + GOV + CREDIT) moves value. Sharing economic identity, governance, and funding across apps gives the aggregate network effects individual apps cannot bootstrap alone.

nodes.label: Dual-token model (GOV vs CREDIT asymmetry)
nodes.rationale: GOV and CREDIT are deliberately asymmetric: GOV is political right, investment gate, and long-term economic weight (fixed 100M cap, captures appreciation via fee-funded buyback); CREDIT is stable operational money 1:1 with USDC (elastic supply, does not vote, not meant to appreciate). Avoids the trap of treating them as symmetric DAO tokens.

nodes.label: Directed staking (per-project curation + investment gate)
nodes.rationale: Unlike generic protocol staking (Uniswap/Aave/Curve), staking GOV requires choosing a project. It buys the right to invest in that project's fundraising round and curation with skin in the game — capital is tied to that project's success. Weight = amount * multiplier(lockDuration), 1x at 14 days to 4x at 365 days. Active selection is part of the model.

nodes.label: Income from real revenue, not emission
nodes.rationale: Since the 2026-07-08 remodel there is no emission as income: investors receive a slice of the funded project's real gross revenue (rev-share deducted by FeeRouterV2 on every pay). Avoids the inflationary spiral of minting unbacked rewards. If nobody uses the apps, there is no income for anyone — tokenomics does not save a bad product.
nodes.norm_label: income from real revenue, not emission

nodes.label: Every political change goes through delay (latency as security)
nodes.rationale: No privileged function of the economic contracts accepts a direct call; all require GOVERNANCE_ROLE held in production only by CommunityTimelock, which only executes Governor-approved proposals after a 2-day delay (172800s). No isolated actor can drain funds or change parameters unilaterally. The ~10-day proposal latency is intentional — latency IS the security mechanism.
nodes.norm_label: every political change goes through delay (latency as security)

nodes.label: Remodel 2026-07-08 (payment rail + rev-share funding)
nodes.rationale: Economic model change from deflationary burn-to-mint to payment rail + rev-share funding. Reason: the old model's ~80% effective take rate for the app could not compete with Stripe/app stores — bypassing was the dominant strategy (Nash equilibrium at collapse; parecer audit/economist/2026-07-08-feerouter-bypass.md). Three new contracts: CreditPSM, FeeRouterV2, ProjectFunding. Burn-to-mint contracts remain deployed for historical compatibility.

nodes.label: Checkpoint anti-flashloan pattern
nodes.rationale: On-chain history of staking weights per block: Staking writes a checkpoint at every change; RewardDistributor reads it at the round's snapshotBlock. Prevents staking in the same block as a query to capture share artificially. Same immunity principle as the Governor's getPastVotes vote snapshot.

nodes.label: Rev-share (1-30% of gross revenue to round investors)
nodes.norm_label: rev-share (1-30% of gross revenue to round investors)

nodes.label: GOV Governance Token
nodes.rationale: Protocol direction and growth capture need a scarce, short-term-non-manipulable instrument with weight proportional to investment; fixed 100M immutable cap, captures value via continuous buyback funded by 40% of the payment fee.

nodes.label: CREDIT Token
nodes.rationale: App pricing needs a stable, predictable currency; CREDIT is 1:1 with USDC via the PSM. No hardcoded supply cap because supply is elastic by design but always 100% USDC-backed (invariant I-PSM1) — a cap would be arbitrary since the real limit is USDC coming in.

nodes.label: Dual-Token Separation Principle
nodes.rationale: Using one token for both governance and payments creates dissonance: either the payment currency floats with governance speculation (ruins app pricing) or spenders get voting rights (ruins separation of powers). CREDIT is a stable payment rail; GOV captures growth.

nodes.label: Directed Staking Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Generic staking creates a passive incentive; directed staking forces stakers to actively select which projects deserve support — decentralized curation with skin in the game. Since the 2026-07-08 remodel it no longer yields emission: it serves curation, investment gate, and governance.

nodes.label: Lock Multiplier (1x-4x, 14-365 days)
nodes.rationale: MAX_LOCK is a saturation point, not a ceiling: locks above 365 days are accepted literally with the multiplier capped at 4x, enabling veCRV-like long commitment signaling without an arbitrary cap.

nodes.label: Staked-GOV Investment Gate
nodes.rationale: invest and claim in ProjectFunding require getWeight(investor, projectId) > 0 — whoever funds is whoever already signaled conviction; unstaking does not forfeit accrued rev-share, the claim is held until re-stake.

nodes.label: Burn-to-Mint Cycle (Legacy Mechanism)
nodes.rationale: Replaced in the 2026-07-08 remodel: the economic analysis audit/economist/2026-07-08-feerouter-bypass.md showed the effective ~80-90% take made bypassing the FeeRouter the dominant strategy for apps, and compensatory emission (alpha*burn) paid investors with inflation, not real value.

nodes.label: Emission Formula min(max(alpha*burn, floor), capMax)
nodes.rationale: alpha < 1 makes total emission < total burn under constant usage (slightly deflationary); alpha range reduced to [0.5, 0.99] so governance can never vote an inflationary value (invariant IE1 by construction).

nodes.label: Floor Schedule (24 declining entries)
nodes.rationale: Bootstrap only: until the ecosystem generates organic burn the DAO underwrites a minimum emission; after 24 rounds (~5.5 months) emission exists only if burn existed — the correct signal for the DAO to intervene if the protocol did not take off.

nodes.label: Probation Penalty (share / 4)
nodes.rationale: New projects carry fraud risk; for 30 days the project receives only 25% of its emission share, and the other 75% is never minted — preserves the deflationary spirit by subtracting emission, not incineration.

nodes.label: Per-Project Sanity Cap (BurnTracker)
nodes.rationale: Prevents a malicious project from burning absurd volume to capture a disproportionate emission share within a round; capMax on total emission limits any residual impact.

nodes.label: V2 Bucket Split 55/25/15/5 (Stakers/LPs/Apps/Bonders)
nodes.rationale: Per-bucket bounds: stakers >= 30%, LPs >= 5%, apps <= 25% (anti self-extraction via wash burn), bonders <= 20% (Olympus showed > 20% unleashes ponzi); split applied after the cap so no bucket exceeds bucketBps * capMax.

nodes.label: Snapshot Block Weighting
nodes.rationale: finalizeRound writes snapshotBlock = block.number and all claim weight queries use that block — the analogue of getPastVotes in ERC20Votes governance, anti-flashloan protection applied to the staking dimension.

nodes.label: Pull-Based Claims
nodes.rationale: No automatic push: avoids gas explosion on rounds with thousands of stakers, delegates gas cost to the beneficiary, enables batch claimMany; the right persists with no deadline.

nodes.label: Separation of Powers (Holders / Governor / Timelock)
nodes.rationale: None of the three components can act alone: the Governor only schedules, the Timelock only executes after delay, holders only vote — total ~10-day window gives any holder time to examine, organize a response, or exit.

nodes.label: Immutable Governance Bounds
nodes.rationale: GOV cap, MIN_LOCK, alpha/capMax ranges and floorSchedule cannot be changed even with 100% of votes — the immutability is a commitment: not even the unanimous DAO can break the rights the user saw at deploy, the trust base that lets stakers immobilize capital.

nodes.label: ProjectRegistry (Whitelist)
nodes.rationale: If anyone could self-include as a project and call burnAndRecord the model would collapse (self-burn to capture rewards); the whitelist places an economic barrier (GOV collateral) and a political one (proposal) — first line of defense against app sybil.

nodes.label: Project Status Lifecycle (Pending/Active/Probation/Removed)
nodes.rationale: Only Removed bypasses the staking lock, because the DAO removed the project and punishing the staker with a lock would be unfair; punitive Probation does not bypass.

nodes.label: GOV Collateral (minCollateral 10,000 GOV)
nodes.rationale: Serves three purposes: entry cost against garbage apps, anti-sybil, and slash mechanism if the app proves fraudulent.

nodes.label: 2-Step Project Ownership Transfer
nodes.rationale: Pending owner has no power until explicit acceptance, protecting against accidental transfer; the new owner should audit appRecipient before accepting because setAppRecipient is owner-gated and a malicious previous owner could hijack the rebate.

nodes.label: Treasury
nodes.rationale: Receives passively, releases only via governance, and deliberately has no pause function — any unilateral power to freeze the treasury would be a capture vector.

nodes.label: FeeRouterV2
nodes.rationale: Sole payment interface in the current model: pay(projectId, amount), 2.5% fee with FEE_BPS_CAP = 500 hard cap not even governance can exceed; atomic, never custodies CREDIT between calls.

nodes.label: PSM Backing Segregation
nodes.rationale: The USDC backing CREDIT is held in the CreditPSM, segregated from the Treasury, with no function to move it — not even via governance: the user's 1:1 redemption right cannot depend on the DAO's budget discipline (invariant I-PSM1).

nodes.label: FFP Buyback (Legacy)
nodes.rationale: Floor-price defence: USDC->CREDIT swap plus immediate burn; bought CREDIT is always burned, never accumulated, because accumulation would create an endogenous capture agent inside the protocol.

nodes.label: Protocol-Owned Liquidity (Legacy)
nodes.rationale: Full-tick range CREDIT/USDC position chosen because concentrated liquidity would require off-chain management; capital-efficient enough for early-stage markets and trivially auditable.

nodes.label: CreditPSM
nodes.rationale: USDC <-> CREDIT 1:1 both directions, backing 100% held with no withdrawal function and no AccessControl of its own — zero admin surface; holds MINTER_ROLE and BURNER_ROLE on CreditToken.

nodes.label: ProjectFunding
nodes.rationale: All-or-nothing funding rounds (rev-share 1-30%, duration 1-90 days, bounds immutable on-chain); invest and claim gated by GOV staked on the project; FeeRouterV2 is the only REVENUE_NOTIFIER.

nodes.label: Anti-Flashloan Snapshots (Two Parallel Rails)
nodes.rationale: Vote (getPastVotes at proposalSnapshot) and reward weight (getWeightAt at snapshotBlock) both use past-block snapshots; an attacker must hold a position at least one block before the reference window, incompatible with same-block flash-loan repayment.

nodes.label: GMV (grossVolumeOf)
nodes.rationale: The single source of everything: app revenue, investor income, protocol fee; GMV at zero for a long time is the terminal symptom.

nodes.label: Rev-Share of Real Revenue
nodes.rationale: No yield from thin air: the CREDIT an investor receives exists because a user paid for the service — a slice of real revenue, not emission; no actor receives value that did not come from an upstream actor.

nodes.label: Vote Delegation (ERC20Votes delegate)
nodes.rationale: Holding balance is not enough — voting power must be activated via delegate(); getPastVotes at the snapshot block makes it flash-loan immune.

nodes.label: Proposal Lifecycle (Pending/Active/Succeeded/Queued/Executed)
nodes.rationale: The v1 Timelock deliberately has no separate guardian or unilateral panic button — no actor can cancel proposals alone, because that would be a capture vector.

nodes.label: PaymentRouted Event
nodes.rationale: The canonical way for an app backend to confirm a payment: decode the receipt and check projectId, payer, and amount — never trust only a frontend callback; the @cesarsst/web3community-sdk implements this flow.

nodes.label: FeeRouterV2.pay(projectId, amount)
nodes.rationale: V2 removed the user parameter: the payer is always msg.sender, so whoever signs the tx is who pays — gas sponsorship requires the user's smart wallet (ERC-4337) to be msg.sender, not an arbitrary relayer.

nodes.label: Ignition Deployments (deployed_addresses.json / dev_addresses.json)
nodes.rationale: Local hardhat node is in-memory: every restart wipes the chain and every redeploy generates new addresses — never hardcode, always read from the JSON or the /config.json served by the frontend.

nodes.label: Project Listing Proposal Process
nodes.rationale: The proposal cannot know the projectId before registerProject assigns it, forcing either two sequential proposals or a single proposal that pre-assumes _nextProjectId (acceptable only at low registration volume).

nodes.label: Preview View Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every mutating function has a side-effect-free preview view (previewPay, pendingRevenue, previewClaim, quote) so UIs can show values before the user signs.

nodes.label: Planned GOV Distribution (30/25/20/15/10)
nodes.rationale: Distribution is proposal intent, not automatic programming: GOV genesis is 0 and each allocation is a separately voted proposal; the Sale, LiquidityBootstrappingPool/LiquidityManager and LPRewards contracts do not exist in the repo yet and must be designed, audited and deployed first.

nodes.label: TeamVesting
nodes.rationale: One instance per beneficiary; 12-month cliff plus linear to 4 years; owner (Timelock) can revoke, freezing the vested boundary and returning the unvested.

nodes.label: Continuous GOV Buyback
nodes.rationale: 40% of every payment's fee (1% of GMV) automatically funds GOV repurchase — buying pressure proportional to real usage, payment by payment, no per-event proposal needed.

nodes.label: Non-Ponzi Design
nodes.rationale: Since the remodel there is no emission as income at all: investor income is a slice of a real user payment, new CREDIT is only born 1:1 against USDC, GOV buyback is funded by a fee on real payments — if usage stops, income dries up immediately with no liability backed by new entrants.

nodes.label: Safeguard Mechanisms (all-or-nothing, gate, hard caps, segregated backing)
nodes.norm_label: safeguard mechanisms (all-or-nothing, gate, hard caps, segregated backing)

nodes.label: App Revenue Risk
nodes.rationale: Investor return in ProjectFunding depends 100% on the app's real revenue; no floor or compensatory emission by design. Mitigated by all-or-nothing rounds with refund, on-chain due-diligence metrics, staked-GOV gate, and hard bounds on rev-share (1-30%) and duration (1-90 days).

nodes.label: PSM Peg/Backing Risk
nodes.rationale: CREDIT is worth 1 USDC only because CreditPSM guarantees 1:1 redemption. Mitigated by 100% backing held in-contract with no withdrawal function (invariant I-PSM1), zero admin surface, and revert-instead-of-partial-pay on insufficient backing. Residual risk: USDC depeg inherited by CREDIT.

nodes.label: Governance Capture Risk
nodes.rationale: An actor accumulating GOV could pass malicious proposals. Mitigated by proposal threshold (10k GOV), 4% quorum, 2-day timelock delay, 7-day voting, on-chain 75% supermajority for Treasury.removePOL and role management on Treasury/Timelock, and on-chain segregation of reserved CREDIT balances.

nodes.label: Flash-Loan Attack Risk (Vote and Reward)
nodes.rationale: Flash loans cannot affect prior-block snapshots: GovernanceToken uses getPastVotes at the proposal snapshot and Staking keeps historic Checkpoints.Trace208 read via getWeightAt at the round snapshotBlock — the reward protection is a direct analog of the governance protection.

nodes.label: Wash-Burn Attack Risk (Legacy)
nodes.rationale: Legacy pre-remodel vector: a project burns self-minted CREDIT to capture emission share. Mitigated by per-(round,project) sanity cap in BurnTracker (10M CREDIT), total capMax per round in RewardDistributor (5M), and 25% probation penalty. With no new emission after the remodel, wash-burn lost its target.

nodes.label: Regulatory Risk
nodes.rationale: Three fronts: rev-share approaches a security (Howey test) — the remodel's most serious regulatory risk; CREDIT as a 1:1 USDC-backed stablecoin may fall under MiCA/US stablecoin regimes; GOV classification as a security via governance-token-with-buyback route. A formal legal opinion is a pre-mainnet blocker.

nodes.label: Gross Volume per Project (GMV) Metric
nodes.rationale: grossVolumeOf on FeeRouterV2 replaces burn as the primary real-usage proxy after the 2026-07-08 remodel; investor income is real revenue, not emission.

nodes.label: Realized Yield per Project Metric
nodes.rationale: cumulative_yield = totalRevenueDistributed / round.raised; annualized against round age. Yield depends 100% on the app's GMV — it is not promised.

nodes.label: PSM Backing Metric (CREDIT Peg)
nodes.rationale: backingNormalized() vs mintedOutstanding(): anyone can verify invariant I-PSM1 at any time; a violation is a critical bug since there is no backing-withdrawal function.

nodes.label: Proposal Lifecycle (8 States)
nodes.rationale: Pending -> Active -> Succeeded/Defeated -> Queued -> Executed/Expired, plus Canceled. Happy path takes ~10 days (1d votingDelay + 7d votingPeriod + 2d timelockMinDelay) — the intentional price of security.

nodes.label: Voting Power (getVotes / getPastVotes)
nodes.rationale: Voting power is not balance: what counts is getPastVotes at the proposal snapshot block, making votes immune to flash loans.

nodes.label: Delegation (ERC20Votes)
nodes.rationale: Delegation is mandatory to activate voting power — ERC20Votes preserves the invariant that the sum of getVotes over delegates equals totalSupply, avoiding vote-stealing patterns and forcing a conscious 'vote myself or delegate' decision.

nodes.label: DAO-Adjustable Parameters
nodes.rationale: Catalog of every governance-adjustable parameter with on-chain bounds hardcoded in setters (e.g. feeBps <= 500, alpha in [0.5, 0.99]); changes take effect at the execution block and affect only future state. Current-rail params are FeeRouterV2 and ProjectFunding; old-rail params remain adjustable but legacy.

nodes.label: Constitutional Floor (Immutable Parameters)
nodes.rationale: Values not even a unanimous DAO can change: GOV 100M cap, staking lock bounds, alpha/capMax bounds, FEE_BPS_CAP 500, rev-share bounds [100,3000] bps, PSM 1:1 no-fee no-withdrawal, the 75% supermajority rule, and the entire CreditPriceOracle configuration.

nodes.label: GovernanceToken (GOV)
nodes.rationale: ERC-20 with ERC20Votes and immutable 100M cap; no pre-mint — supply starts at zero and every distribution happens via DAO proposals calling mint. Not burnable. Owner in production is CommunityTimelock via Ownable2Step.

nodes.label: CreditToken (CREDIT)
nodes.rationale: Utility ERC-20 with elastic supply and no hardcoded cap; MINTER_ROLE and BURNER_ROLE are plural by design to allow V1->V2 migrations. Deliberately does not inherit ERC20Votes — CREDIT does not vote, keeping governance separate from operational use.

nodes.label: burnByRole Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Role-gated burn without allowance enables the 1-tx FeeRouter.pay -> BurnTracker.burnAndRecord -> burnByRole path; a burnFrom flow would need two txs and open a front-run window between approve and burn. Safe because the role is only granted to specific contracts via proposal + Timelock.

nodes.label: ProjectRegistry
nodes.rationale: On-chain whitelist and single source of truth for project ownership, GOV collateral (skin in the game), status (Pending/Active/Probation/Removed) and metadata. Two distinct probation notions coexist: initial time-based (reward penalty) and punitive status.

nodes.label: ownerRecipient 48h Timelock
nodes.rationale: Without a timelock the project owner could hot-swap the apps-bucket recipient between finalizeRound and off-chain indexing, diverting the bucket to a hostile address. 48h matches the DAO's ~2-day proposal cycle; cancelOwnerRecipient is available to owner and governance as an escape hatch for compromised keys.

nodes.label: Treasury
nodes.rationale: DAO multi-asset custody; only outflow path is GOVERNANCE_ROLE (invariant I4). Deliberately has no pause — unilateral freeze power would be a capture vector. Post-CLP it also executes the FFP buyback, provisions POL, and keeps Phase 1.4 reserved ledgers.

nodes.label: FFP Buyback (Floor Price Defence)
nodes.rationale: Real USDC->CREDIT swap via Uniswap V3 with immediate burn when spot TWAP stays below the floor (max of 50% MA90 and $0.10) for 24h, with Chainlink USDC/USD sanity, per-event (20%) and monthly (30% of snapshot) caps. Bought CREDIT is always burned: accumulating it would make the Treasury an endogenous capture agent and distort demand signals. Monthly cap uses a snapshot so reserve donations cannot inflate the remaining ceiling.

nodes.label: Protocol-Owned Liquidity (POL)
nodes.rationale: CREDIT/USDC full-range Uniswap V3 position with the NFT custodied by the Treasury itself. Full range chosen (audit/economist/2026-04-24-pol-params.md) because it needs no active rebalance, is capital-efficient enough early-stage, and is trivially auditable; every removePOL requires a 75% supermajority in the Governor.

nodes.label: On-chain CREDIT Reserved-Balance Segregation
nodes.rationale: polRefillBucket + pendingGaugeRewards <= balanceOf(CREDIT), enforced on both sides: generic outflows revert with TransferExceedsUnreservedCredit and ledger deposits revert with DepositExceedsCreditBalance so a compromised depositor cannot inflate the reserve beyond backing. writeDown* valves exist because the bonders bucket grows in CREDIT with no on-chain USDC counterpart and would otherwise grow monotonically.

nodes.label: Staking
nodes.rationale: Roleless vault for GOV staking directed per project; weight = amount x multiplier(lockDuration). Three checkpoint rails (user-project, project, global) updated in O(1) via diffs to avoid iterating stakers. Unstake bypasses lock only when the project is Removed.

nodes.label: Lock Multiplier Formula (1x-4x)
nodes.rationale: Linear from 1e18 at 14 days to 4e18 at 365 days, saturating at 4x for longer locks. stake consolidation resets lockStartAt intentionally so micro-stakes cannot extend weight without re-committing the old amount; increaseStake preserves the lock.

nodes.label: BurnTracker (Legacy)
nodes.rationale: Internal oracle accounting CREDIT burn per (round, projectId); burnAndRecord burns atomically via burnByRole — off-chain listeners and record-without-burn alternatives were rejected (trusted-indexer window, trivial double-spend). closeRound is governance-gated because permissionless close could be timed to favour a project. Legacy after the 2026-07-08 remodel.

nodes.label: RewardDistributor (V1, Legacy)
nodes.rationale: V1 emission distributor: single stakers bucket, pull-based claim minting CREDIT on demand; per-project emission computed at claim to scale gas with claim count. In claim-only mode during the 4-round V2 migration window; after the cutoff governance revokes its MINTER_ROLE and unclaimed V1 rewards become unmintable — intentional.

nodes.label: Emission Formula min(max(alpha*burn, floor), capMax)
nodes.rationale: emission_R = min(max(alpha * burn_{R-1}, floor(R)), capMax). MAX_ALPHA reduced from 1.1e18 to 0.99e18 to enforce invariant IE1 (alpha < 1 permanent) by construction — see audit/economist/2026-04-22-consistency-audit.md C2. floorSchedule is an immutable 24-entry decaying bootstrap floor.

nodes.label: RewardDistributorV2 (Legacy)
nodes.rationale: Bucket-aware distributor of CLP Phase 1.4, parallel deploy alongside V1. Stakers stay pull-based (thousands of claimants — push would explode gas) while LPs/apps/bonders are push (O(1) or O(N projects)); apps are rewarded by retrospective burn because Phase 1 has no gauge controller and burn is already a real usage signal.

nodes.label: 4-Bucket Emission Split (Stakers/LPs/Apps/Bonders)
nodes.rationale: Default [5500, 2500, 1500, 500] bps applied AFTER the cap (IE3 strengthened). Per-bucket bounds: stakers >= 30% preserves the economic signal, LPs >= 5% (IE6), apps <= 25% (IE4b anti self-extraction via wash burn), bonders <= 20% because Olympus showed more unleashes ponzi dynamics. Bonders absorbs integer-division residue (IE12, 3 wei tolerance).

nodes.label: FeeRouter (V1, Legacy)
nodes.rationale: Legacy single payment interface splitting every CREDIT payment into burn/treasury/rebate (production 70/20/10). pay is public to allow user-direct, app-sponsored and relayer/AA flows — the economic payer is always the user via transferFrom. No custody between calls; router ends every pay with balance 0.

nodes.label: FeeRouterV2
nodes.rationale: Payment rail of the 2026-07-08 remodel: 2.5% fee (hard cap 5%) split 40% treasury / 40% GOV buyback / 20% grants, plus project rev-share to ProjectFunding, remainder (~89.5-97.5%) instantly to the app. No burn, no emission — fee is competitive with payment processors (below Stripe ~3.8%) versus the ~80% effective take rate of V1 (audit/economist/2026-07-08-feerouter-bypass.md). grossVolumeOf is the on-chain GMV metric for investors.

nodes.label: CommunityTimelock
nodes.rationale: Identity wrapper over OZ TimelockController (minDelay 2 days), self-administered post-handoff, sole holder of GOVERNANCE_ROLE/DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE across the economic contracts. EXECUTOR_ROLE is address(0) — the delay is already the security gate, so anyone may execute; CANCELLER_ROLE is Governor-only because an external canceller could DoS valid proposals.

nodes.label: CommunityGovernor
nodes.rationale: Canonical Governor on the OZ 5.0.2 stack (Settings, CountingSimple, Votes, QuorumFraction, TimelockControl). Production: votingDelay 7200 blocks, votingPeriod 50400, threshold 10k GOV, quorum 4%. propose scans targets/calldatas and classifies ProposalType; TREASURY is immutable in the constructor.

nodes.label: 75% Supermajority Rule (removePOL / Role Management)
nodes.rationale: Previously a cultural norm, made code in Phase 1.2: proposals containing Treasury.removePOL or grantRole/revokeRole/renounceRole targeting the Treasury or the Timelock require forVotes >= 3x againstVotes AND forVotes > 0 (closes the abstain-only quorum edge case). A mixed batch contaminates the whole proposal by design — otherwise packing the sensitive call with popular ones would dilute the requirement. Conservative: every removePOL requires 75% regardless of fraction, because POL liquidity changes between propose and execute making proportional checks evadable. Role-management scanning closes the re-authorization bypass (granting Treasury or Timelock roles to a third party who could call removePOL directly).

nodes.label: TeamVesting
nodes.rationale: Linear vesting vault with cliff, one instance per team member so revoking one does not affect others and each schedule is individually auditable. Ownable2Step instead of AccessControl because revocation authority is inherently singular (DAO via Timelock). Revoke is one-shot and freezes the vested boundary; release stays pull-based.

nodes.label: UserSubsidy
nodes.rationale: Distributes pre-funded CREDIT to first app users via Merkle drops with claim caps, subsidizing demand during ~6-month bootstrap. msg.sender is the mandatory recipient to block claim-on-behalf sybil harvesting; budget is implicit (fungible tokens make per-campaign reservation a false guarantee).

nodes.label: Merkle Drop Campaign
nodes.rationale: Eligibility selection stays off-chain; only the compacted Merkle root goes on-chain via proposal — the DAO approves the root, not the selection logic. OZ double-hash leaf (keccak256(bytes.concat(keccak256(abi.encode(user))))) prevents second-preimage attacks on intermediate nodes.

nodes.label: LiquidityGauge (Legacy)
nodes.rationale: Adapter over the canonical UniswapV3Staker distributing the LPs bucket of per-round emission to CREDIT/USDC LPs (CLP Phase 1.3) — it does not reinvent NFT custody or in-range accounting. pause blocks entry only; unstake/harvest and emergencyUnstake stay operational (IE10 fail-safe). Treasury/Staking/RewardDistributor/FeeRouter are denylisted at bootstrap (anti self-dealing D.9).

nodes.label: UniswapV3Staker (Canonical)
nodes.rationale: Uniswap Foundation canonical staker (mainnet 0xe34139463bA50bD61336E0c446Bd8C0867c6fE65); owns all NFT custody and secondsInsideX128 in-range accounting the gauge relies on.

nodes.label: Gauge Vesting Segregation (totalVestingLocked)
nodes.rationale: 14-day linear vesting on unstaked rewards, accumulating independently of whether the NFT remains staked (rewards were already earned at the official staker). totalVestingLocked is untouchable by governanceRescueRewards — the rescue only reaches getUnreservedBalance(), protecting users' vesting on-chain.

nodes.label: CreditPriceOracle
nodes.rationale: Dumb, deterministic ICreditPriceOracle adapter: Uniswap V3 CREDIT/USDC TWAP converted to real USD via Chainlink USDC/USD (6h staleness, fixed [9900,10100] sanity band). No owner, no setters, no mutable storage — any parameter change requires a new deploy plus Treasury.setPriceOracle. TWAP window is a call parameter so tuning the buyback window never requires re-deploying the oracle. GPL-2.0-or-later due to the TickMath port.

nodes.label: CreditPSM
nodes.rationale: Peg Stability Module of the 2026-07-08 remodel: USDC <-> CREDIT at exact 1:1, no fee, both directions. CREDIT stops being speculative/deflationary and becomes a stable payment rail; ecosystem appreciation migrates to GOV via the FeeRouterV2-funded buyback. No owner, no roles of its own, no setters — zero admin surface; it only needs MINTER_ROLE and BURNER_ROLE on the CreditToken.

nodes.label: Invariant I-PSM1 (Full Backing)
nodes.rationale: USDC.balanceOf(psm) >= mintedOutstanding in normalized units, verifiable by anyone at any time; there is no backing-withdrawal function, not even for governance. mintedOutstanding is a conservative estimate (clamped at zero when legacy CREDIT is sold) — the verifiable real backing is always backing().

nodes.label: ProjectFunding
nodes.rationale: Funding-rounds contract of the remodel: all-or-nothing rounds with refund, rev-share bounded [100,3000] bps and duration [1,90] days; FeeRouterV2 holds REVENUE_NOTIFIER_ROLE and is the only address authorized to call notifyRevenue.

nodes.label: BurnTracker
nodes.rationale: Atomic on-chain burnAndRecord chosen over off-chain event listener (indexer dependency, burn/record race) and app self-reporting (trivial double-spend). closeRound is governance-gated because permissionless close would let anyone time round closure to favor a specific project. Tracker never calls the distributor (pull-based reads) to avoid cyclic coupling. LEGACY after remodel 2026-07-08: payments no longer burn CREDIT; usage metric is now FeeRouterV2.grossVolumeOf.

nodes.label: RewardDistributor V1
nodes.rationale: Emission formula min(max(alpha*burn, floor), capMax) with per-project share computed lazily in claim so gas scales with claims, not projects. MAX_ALPHA reduced to 0.99e18 to guarantee IE1 (alpha<1) by construction. Fixed uint256[24] floorSchedule forces exactly 24 values and is immutable post-constructor. LEGACY: claim-only during 4-round CLP migration window, MINTER_ROLE revoked after cutoff.

nodes.label: RewardDistributorV2
nodes.rationale: Bucket-aware distributor (CLP Fase 1.4): stakers 55% pull (thousands of stakers -> push would explode gas), LPs 25% push O(1) via gauge notifyRewardAmount, apps 15% push by retrospective burn signal (no gauge controller until Phase 2), bonders 5% push to Treasury POL refill. Split applied AFTER cap (IE3 strengthened); bonders absorb integer-division residue (IE12, 3 wei tolerance). Gauge-paused fallback deposits to Treasury so pausing the gauge cannot brick finalizeRound. Apps recipient changes require 48h Registry timelock to prevent hot-swap between finalize and off-chain indexing. LEGACY after remodel 2026-07-08.

nodes.label: FeeRouter V1
nodes.rationale: Single payment interface splitting each pay() into burn/treasury/rebate (production Fase 0 default 70/20/10). pay is public to enable user-direct, app-sponsored, and relayer/AA flows; economic payer is always `user` via transferFrom. No sweep function: router holds zero balance between calls, and adding sweep would create a centralization surface. REPLACED by FeeRouterV2 because ~80% effective take rate made bypassing the router the dominant strategy (audit/economist/2026-07-08-feerouter-bypass.md).

nodes.label: FeeRouterV2
nodes.rationale: Payment rail of the 2026-07-08 remodel: 2.5% protocol fee (hard cap FEE_BPS_CAP=500 that not even governance can exceed), fee split 40/40/20 treasury/buyback/grants, rev-share deducted per ProjectFunding.revShareBpsOf, remainder (~97.5%) to the app in the same tx. No burn, no emission. Transfer-then-notify: rev-share CREDIT is transferred to ProjectFunding BEFORE notifyRevenue so the accumulator never counts absent funds. Unlike V1, integration needs no roles: approve + pay.

nodes.label: CommunityTimelock
nodes.rationale: Identity wrapper over OZ TimelockController 5.0.2 with zero extra code (keeps on-chain name without new attack surface). minDelay 2 days as reaction window. Executor is address(0) (anyone) because operation params are immutable after schedule and the delay is the real gate; a dedicated executor would only add friction. CANCELLER_ROLE only for the Governor: an external canceller/guardian could DoS valid proposals, violating 'the vote is the source of truth'. Self-administered post-handoff; no pause button by design.

nodes.label: CommunityGovernor
nodes.rationale: Canonical OZ 5.0.2 Governor stack (Settings, CountingSimple, Votes, VotesQuorumFraction, TimelockControl). Voting power from GovernanceToken ERC20Votes past snapshots (flash-loan immune); quorum 4% of past total supply; EIP-712 name 'CommunityGovernor' is immutable because renaming would invalidate all past signatures. Clock in blocks (block.number).

nodes.label: TeamVesting
nodes.rationale: Linear vesting with cliff for a single beneficiary; one instance per team member so revocation is isolated and accounting auditable. Ownable2Step instead of AccessControl because revocation authority is inherently singular (DAO via Timelock) and 2-step protects against wrong-address ownership transfer. revoke does NOT auto-transfer vested funds (pull UX, avoids surprise transfers to offline multisigs). start may be in the past to recognize pre-TGE service.

nodes.label: UserSubsidy
nodes.rationale: Merkle-drop CREDIT campaigns subsidizing demand during bootstrap. Merkle root (not per-app signatures) keeps user-selection logic off-chain: DAO approves the root, not the logic. Double-hashed leaves (OZ standard) prevent second-preimage on intermediate nodes. msg.sender is forcibly the recipient to block sybil operators claiming for inattentive users. Budget is implicit (no per-campaign reservation) because tokens are fungible and reservation adds overhead without real guarantees.

nodes.label: LiquidityGauge
nodes.rationale: Adapter over the canonical UniswapV3Staker (CLP Fase 1.3) instead of reinventing NFT custody or secondsInsideX128 accounting. Rewards vest linearly 14 days after unstake; vesting accrues independently of the NFT remaining staked (rewards were already earned). pause blocks entry only, never exit (IE10); emergencyUnstake works even when paused (forfeits current-cycle rewards). Denylist prevents self-dealing by Treasury/protocol contracts (D.9). LEGACY after remodel 2026-07-08 (LP bucket gone); remains for unstake/harvest of remaining positions.

nodes.label: CreditPriceOracle
nodes.rationale: Dumb deterministic adapter deriving CREDIT/USD TWAP (18 dec) from the Uniswap V3 CREDIT/USDC pool, converted to real USD via Chainlink USDC/USD. No owner, no setters, no mutable storage: any config change means new deploy + Treasury.setPriceOracle. TWAP window is a call parameter so tuning the buyback window never requires oracle redeploy. Fixed Chainlink sanity band [9900,10100] bps mirrors Treasury defaults as defense-in-depth for recordDailyPrice (which skips the Treasury's own check). address(0) feed = deliberate 1 USDC = 1 USD fallback for networks without the feed. GPL-2.0-or-later due to TickMath port.

nodes.label: CreditPSM
nodes.rationale: Peg Stability Module: USDC <-> CREDIT 1:1, no fee. Pillar of the 2026-07-08 remodel — CREDIT becomes a stable payment rail, 100% backed. No fee because the PSM is infrastructure, not revenue (monetization lives in FeeRouterV2); a conversion fee would weaken the peg. NO backing-withdrawal function exists, not even for governance (I-PSM1); no owner, no roles, no pause. sell rejects dust below 1e12 wei instead of confiscating it (I-PSM2). Legacy pre-remodel CREDIT is redeemable only up to actually-deposited backing (InsufficientBacking + conservative counter clamp).

nodes.label: ProjectFunding
nodes.rationale: All-or-nothing funding rounds (target in CREDIT, rev-share 1%-30%, 1-90 days): owner is only paid when raised == target exactly (ExceedsTarget forbids overshoot), protecting investors from half-funding an unviable project; Failed rounds refund 100%. MasterChef accumulator gives O(1) notifyRevenue and O(1) claim with no investor loops. GOV-staked gate on invest AND claim materializes 'skin in the game'; unclaimed revenue never expires, it just stays inaccessible until re-stake. One round per project in the MVP (stacking share pools with different bps deferred to V2).

nodes.label: Treasury
nodes.rationale: Fase 1.1 replaced the executeBuyback stub with a real FFP buyback-and-burn (governance-only, nonReentrant), permissionless recordDailyPrice with 22h cooldown, and bounded FFP setters. Buyback reverts with BuybackInfraMissing until oracle/router/feeTier/Chainlink infra is set — fail-safe by default. MA90 floor requires 90 recorded days before the 0.50x multiplier dominates (anti early-manipulation); until then floor = absolute $0.10.

nodes.label: Uniswap V3 TickMath / OracleLibrary port
nodes.rationale: Faithful 0.8.24 port of TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick (v3-core 0.7.6, GPL-2.0-or-later); only adaptations are an unchecked block (algorithm relies on controlled wrap-around) and custom errors. _quoteAtTick follows OracleLibrary.getQuoteAtTick using OZ Math.mulDiv instead of Uniswap FullMath.

nodes.label: Mainnet Deployment Procedure
nodes.rationale: 4-phase gated procedure (F0 pre-deploy audit/multisig/monitoring, F1 deploy with Ignition sub-phases A-D, F2 governance bootstrap, F3 distribution, F4 handoff). Deployer renounces DEFAULT_ADMIN last in phase D or it loses power to grant the rest. Genesis mint happens before renouncing admin on CreditToken.

nodes.label: Security Model
nodes.rationale: Consolidates invariants I1-I7 (legacy) and remodel invariants (I-PSM1/2, fee hard cap, pay conservation, all-or-nothing, GOV gate, transfer-then-notify), attack surfaces and threat model. Deliberate absences: no rescueTokens (would be a governance-accessible backdoor), no proxies/upgrades, no pause, no unilateral guardian in v1 — Timelock delay is the residual mitigation even against >50% capture.

nodes.label: Recursos (referencias externas)
nodes.rationale: Catalogs OZ 5.0.2 contracts used, EIPs (20/2612/5805/712/165), tooling (Hardhat, Ignition, Slither, Defender, Forta, Tenderly) and architectural inspirations: Uniswap, Aave, Compound, MakerDAO, Optimism, Curve (veCRV gauges inspired directed staking).

nodes.label: Fase 0 CLP: setDefaultSplit 70/20/10
nodes.rationale: First DAO proposal of the CLP pivot and hard gate for Fase 1: move FeeRouter default split 95/0/5 -> 70/20/10. 20% treasury creates recurring DAO revenue (resolves C4: Treasury without recurring income, blocking the Fase 1 flywheel); 70% keeps I2 burn-on-consumption; 10% doubles app rebate. As of 2026-07 the split is baked into deploy parameters, so the on-chain proposal is only needed on networks deployed with the old split.

nodes.label: Remodel 2026-07-08 (payment rail + rev-share)
nodes.rationale: Protocol pivoted from burn-to-mint deflation (70% of each payment burned + reward emission) to a stable payment rail + rev-share funding model. Motive: ~80% effective take rate could not compete with Stripe (~3.8%), so bypassing the router was the dominant strategy (audit/economist/2026-07-08-feerouter-bypass.md). New core: CreditPSM (1:1 USDC), FeeRouterV2 (2.5% fee, 40/40/20), ProjectFunding (rev-share 1-30%). Legacy contracts remain on-chain, marked LEGADO, serving only historical claims.

nodes.label: Credit Liquidity Protocol (CLP) Pivot
nodes.rationale: Two-phase pivot with hard gate (user decision 2026-04-24): Fase 0 default split 70/20/10 unlocks Treasury revenue; Fase 1.1 FFP buyback, 1.2 POL, 1.3 LiquidityGauge, 1.4 bucket-aware RewardDistributorV2; Fase 3 bonding (BondDepository) planned as structural POL refill.

nodes.label: FFP (Floating con Floor Price defendido)
nodes.rationale: CREDIT peg model: floor = max(0.50 x MA90, $0.10 absolute), defended by Treasury buyback-and-burn only after a 24h sustained breach, with per-event (20% reserves) and monthly (30%) caps and 1% max slippage. The ~10-day governance latency is a feature: impulsive buybacks inside a continuous crash are how Iron Finance / OHM died. Buyback is blocked while USDC is depegged (buying CREDIT with depegged USDC destroys reserves — cross death-spiral vector). Hibernation mode when reserves run out relies on organic burn-by-use.

nodes.label: Protocol Owned Liquidity (POL)
nodes.rationale: Treasury becomes permanent full-range LP of the Uniswap V3 CREDIT/USDC pool: without pool liquidity, executeBuyback swaps against an empty book. Seed proposal must be a single atomic executeBatch (grant MINTER -> mint pol-seed -> revoke -> addPOL) or a governance attacker could front-run the authorized mint with a fake pool. Known two-sided risk: each buyback drains the POL's USDC side; structural mitigation (bonding) only arrives in Fase 3, until then monitor composition and pause buybacks if POL exceeds ~80% CREDIT. Soft cap norm: 30-50% pool share, >50% needs explicit justification.

nodes.label: Supermajority 75% gate for removePOL
nodes.rationale: Enforced on-chain in CommunityGovernor: propose() scans the batch and marks any proposal containing Treasury.removePOL (selector 0x6a71d4b3) — or role-management calls targeting Treasury or the Timelock (closing the re-authorization bypass) — as ProposalType.Supermajority; _voteSucceeded then requires forVotes >= 3 x againstVotes AND forVotes > 0. Conservative by design: the removed fraction is not measurable at propose time, so ANY removal takes the strict gate; mixed batches are contaminated.

nodes.label: Burn-to-mint (modelo legado)
nodes.rationale: Legacy economic model: CREDIT consumed in payments is burned (deflation) and next-round emission is minted to stakers proportionally to per-project burn. Replaced by the 2026-07-08 remodel because the effective take rate made router bypass dominant.

nodes.label: Anti-flashloan snapshot protection
nodes.rationale: Two protected dimensions: (1) voting reads getPastVotes at the proposal snapshot block; (2) stake weight reads Staking.getWeightAt at roundData.snapshotBlock via Checkpoints.Trace208. A flash loan borrows and repays in the same block, so the attacker's position at the snapshot is zero — holding for at least one prior block is required, which flash loans cannot do.

nodes.label: CEI + ReentrancyGuard double pattern
nodes.rationale: All value-moving contracts apply both Checks-Effects-Interactions ordering AND ReentrancyGuard. The guard is defense-in-depth: CEI alone suffices for known ERC-20s, but arbitrary tokens (Treasury accepts any ERC-20) may have hooks, and the guard also prevents future regressions. Cost ~2k gas on the happy path, acceptable for 100k+ gas operations.

nodes.label: DAO bootstrap paradox
nodes.rationale: Canonical ERC20Votes + Timelock dilemma: changing state needs a proposal, proposing needs delegated GOV above threshold, having GOV needs a mint, and minting is itself a state change. Between deploy and the Timelock's acceptOwnership the deployer holds sovereign mint power. Mitigations: multisig deployer (4-of-7), minimal bootstrap mint (~12k GOV, just above the 10k threshold, never the full 100M), and acceptOwnership as the very first proposal.

nodes.label: MasterChef accumulator pattern
nodes.rationale: accRevenuePerShare += amount * 1e18 / raised on each revenue notification; investor claim = shares * acc / 1e18 - rewardDebt. Gives O(1) per payment and O(1) per claim with no loops over investors.

nodes.label: CommunityTimelock
nodes.rationale: Wrapper identitario sobre TimelockController OZ 5.0.2 sem codigo adicional: mantem identidade on-chain (nome no Etherscan) sem superficie extra. Executor = address(0) porque parametros ja sao imutaveis apos schedule e o delay e o gate de seguranca; exigir EXECUTOR_ROLE dedicado so adicionaria friccao. CANCELLER_ROLE exclusivo do Governor: cancelador externo poderia DoSar propostas validas, violando 'o voto e a fonte de verdade'. Sem pause unilateral; self-administered pos-handoff, upgrade exige multiplas propostas por design.

nodes.label: CommunityGovernor
nodes.rationale: Governor canonico OZ 5.0.2 (Settings, CountingSimple, Votes, VotesQuorumFraction, TimelockControl). Constructor ganhou argumento treasury imutavel (Fase 1.2 CLP) para o scan de propose que aplica supermaioria 75%. name EIP-712 imutavel: renomear invalidaria todas as assinaturas passadas. Clock em blocos (block.number), quorum sobre getPastTotalSupply do snapshot para imunidade a manipulacao de supply.

nodes.label: Supermaioria 75% para remocao de POL
nodes.rationale: Norma cultural virou codigo (Fase 1.2 CLP): propostas contendo Treasury.removePOL ou gestao de roles no Treasury/Timelock exigem forVotes >= 3*againstVotes E forVotes > 0. Batch misto contamina a proposta inteira — correto por design, senao empacotar a call sensivel junto de calls populares diluiria o requisito de 75%. Conservador por design: a fracao '>25% do POL' nao e medida no propose porque a liquidez muda entre propose e execute, tornando qualquer check proporcional burlavel. Scan de grantRole/revokeRole/renounceRole fecha vetores de re-autorizacao. Guard forVotes > 0 fecha edge case de quorum atingido so com Abstain.

nodes.label: TeamVesting
nodes.rationale: Vesting linear com cliff, um unico beneficiario por instancia: isolamento de revogacao, contabilidade 1 instancia = 1 cronograma, parametros individuais. Ownable2Step em vez de AccessControl porque a autoridade de revogacao e inerentemente singular (DAO via Timelock) e o 2-step protege contra transferencia errada. Pull-based release (evita transferencia surpresa a multisig offline); revoke one-shot congela fronteira em totalAllocatedAtRevoke; start no passado permitido deliberadamente (reconhecimento de servico pre-TGE); sem pause — 'pausar' = revoke, semanticamente mais honesto.

nodes.label: UserSubsidy
nodes.rationale: Subsidia demanda (nao oferta) no bootstrap ~6 meses via Merkle drops de CREDIT com cap de claims. msg.sender = recipient obrigatorio (sem parametro 'to') para impedir claim-em-nome-de-outro por sybil operators. Budget implicito (sem reserva por campanha) porque tokens sao fungiveis e reservar nao garante nada contra mis-funding. closeCampaign antes do deadline permitido para emergencias (merkle comprometido), com aviso implicito de 2 dias via timelock. credit imutavel: um UserSubsidy = um token.

nodes.label: Distribuicao por Merkle Campaign
nodes.rationale: Merkle (nao assinatura por app) mantem a logica de selecao de usuarios off-chain: so a raiz compactada entra on-chain via proposta — DAO aprova a raiz, nao a logica. Double-hash do leaf (keccak256(bytes.concat(keccak256(abi.encode(user))))) e padrao OZ contra second-preimage em nos intermediarios.

nodes.label: LiquidityGauge
nodes.rationale: LEGADO pos-remodel 2026-07-08 (substituido por CreditPSM/FeeRouterV2/ProjectFunding), mantido deployado por compatibilidade. Adapter sobre o UniswapV3Staker canonico em vez de custodia propria: nao reinventa custodia de NFT nem duplica secondsInsideX128. Pause bloqueia apenas ENTRADA (IE10 'nao pausar usuario'); emergencyUnstake fail-safe sempre operacional mas descarta rewards do ciclo. Vesting acumula independente do NFT continuar staked: rewards ja foram ganhos no staker oficial. Denylist anti self-dealing (D.9) para Treasury/Staking/RewardDistributor/FeeRouter.

nodes.label: Segregacao on-chain de vesting (totalVestingLocked)
nodes.rationale: totalVestingLocked segrega o CREDIT que lastreia VestingPositions nao sacadas: governanceRescueRewards so alcanca getUnreservedBalance() (RescueExceedsUnreserved). Antes era norma contabil off-chain; agora e invariante enforced (I8, CLP Fase 1.4).

nodes.label: CreditPriceOracle
nodes.rationale: Adapter burro e deterministico por desenho: SEM owner, SEM setters, SEM storage mutavel — mudar pool/feed/banda = novo deploy + Treasury.setPriceOracle. Janela TWAP e parametro da chamada (Treasury decide twapWindowSecs), entao ajustar a janela do buyback nao exige re-deploy. Banda de sanidade Chainlink fixa [9900,10100] bps = defesa em profundidade para recordDailyPrice, que nao passa pela checagem do Treasury. Fallback 1 USDC = 1 USD quando feed = address(0), deliberado para redes sem feed; saida em USD real para que depeg do USDC nao passe silencioso. GPL-2.0-or-later por conter port fiel do TickMath da Uniswap V3.

nodes.label: Port TickMath/OracleLibrary (Uniswap V3)
nodes.rationale: Port fiel do TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick (v3-core 0.7.6) para 0.8.24: unica adaptacao e o bloco unchecked (wrap-around controlado) e custom error no lugar de require 'T'. _quoteAtTick segue OracleLibrary.getQuoteAtTick usando Math.mulDiv do OZ (512 bits) no lugar do FullMath.

nodes.label: CreditPSM
nodes.rationale: Peg Stability Module do remodel 2026-07-08: USDC <-> CREDIT 1:1 sem taxa nos dois sentidos. CREDIT deixa de ser ativo especulativo/deflacionario e vira trilho de pagamento estavel, 100% lastreado no USDC retido no proprio contrato. NENHUMA funcao de saque do lastro — nem governanca; DAO gasta da fee do FeeRouterV2, nunca daqui. Sem owner, roles proprias ou parametros ajustaveis. DustAmount reverte em vez de confiscar poeira; mintedOutstanding e estimativa conservadora com clamp em zero. Quem captura valorizacao agora e o GOV (buyback via fee do FeeRouterV2); pool DEX e FFP viram legado.

nodes.label: ProjectFunding
nodes.rationale: Remodel 2026-07-08: substitui a emissao inflacionaria de CREDIT como fonte de renda do investidor — quem financia compra fatia (revShareBps 1-30%) da receita bruta futura paga pelo FeeRouterV2. All-or-nothing: dono so recebe se bater o alvo, protegendo o investidor de financiar pela metade um projeto inviavel. Skin in the game: invest e claim exigem GOV stakeado no projeto (Staking.getWeight > 0) — alinha funding com curadoria; sem stake o valor nao se perde, fica acruado ate re-stake. Uma rodada por projeto (MVP); bounds imutaveis rev-share [1%,30%], prazo [1,90] dias. Yield transparente calculavel on-chain.

nodes.label: Padrao MasterChef (accRevenuePerShare)
nodes.rationale: Acumulador de receita por share com precisao 1e18 e rewardDebt por investidor: distribuicao O(1) por pagamento e O(1) por claim, sem iterar investidores.

nodes.label: Anti-flashloan em duas dimensoes (voto + peso de stake)
nodes.rationale: Voto: getPastVotes no snapshotBlock (ERC20Votes) — flash-loan pega e devolve no mesmo bloco, posicao no snapshot e zero. Peso de stake: RewardDistributor._calculateClaim le Staking.getWeightAt no snapshotBlock gravado em finalizeRound — flash-stake no bloco da finalize nao entra. Checkpoints.Trace208: uint48 para block.number, uint208 para valor (peso maximo teorico 4e26 << 2^208).
nodes.norm_label: anti-flashloan em duas dimensoes (voto + peso de stake)

nodes.label: Burn atomico via BURNER_ROLE
nodes.rationale: Alternativas rejeitadas: (a) event listener off-chain — depende de indexer confiavel, sem prova on-chain, race conditions; (b) app registra sem queimar — double-spend trivial. Adotada: atomic on-chain via burnByRole sem allowance, porque exigir allowance quebraria UX (duas txs + janela de front-run). Mitigacao: BURNER_ROLE so via proposta Governor+Timelock, revocavel.

nodes.label: Probation duplo (inicial por tempo vs punitiva)
nodes.rationale: Duas nocoes coexistem no ProjectRegistry: probation inicial automatica (isInProbation view, projeto Active, share 25% via penalty /4) e probation punitiva (status Probation, isActive=false, share zero, sem stake/pagamento/burn novos). A penalty de 25% e aplicada no RewardDistributor no claim e nao se aplica a punitiva.
nodes.norm_label: probation duplo (inicial por tempo vs punitiva)

nodes.label: Paradoxo do bootstrap DAO
nodes.rationale: Problema canonico de DAO ERC20Votes+Timelock: mudar estado exige proposta, propor exige GOV delegado, ter GOV exige mint, mintar e mudanca de estado. Solucao: deployer (multi-sig auditavel) faz mint minimo e transferOwnership(timelock); primeira proposta mainnet DEVE ser acceptOwnership() pelo Timelock. Janela critica deploy->acceptOwnership mitigada por multisig, priorizacao da primeira proposta e renuncia planejada.

nodes.label: Padrao duplo CEI + ReentrancyGuard
nodes.rationale: CEI sozinho bastaria para tokens conhecidos (GOV/CREDIT sem callbacks), mas o Treasury recebe ERC-20 arbitrario (hooks ERC-777/maliciosos) — guard e defesa em profundidade e evita regressoes futuras. Custo ~2k gas em operacoes de 100k+, aceitavel.

nodes.label: Floor decay — 24 entradas imutaveis
nodes.rationale: floorSchedule uint256[24] fixo no constructor do RewardDistributor: forca o caller a passar 24 valores e e imutavel pos-deploy. Decaimento linear de 400k a ~16.7k CREDIT em 24 rodadas; soma da serie = 5M CREDIT (+184 wei de dust), safety net bem abaixo do genesis de 10M.

nodes.label: Checkpoints globais de peso no Staking
nodes.rationale: Tres trilhos paralelos (_userWeight, _projectWeight, _globalWeightCheckpoints) atualizados em O(1) por escrita; invariante globalWeight == SUM(projectWeight). Motivacao: RewardDistributor precisa projectWeight/globalWeight no bootstrap — sem agregado global O(1) seria preciso iterar N projetos por finalize, inviavel em gas.
nodes.norm_label: checkpoints globais de peso no staking

nodes.label: Split default 70/20/10 (Fase 0 CLP)
nodes.rationale: defaultSplit do FeeRouter nao e hardcoded — vem de ignition/parameters/production.json. Fase 0 do CLP mudou para (7000,2000,1000) 70% burn / 20% treasury / 10% rebate para dar ao Treasury fonte recorrente de CREDIT (lado CREDIT do refill de POL) sem depender so de bootstrap externo; burn ainda domina para preservar o incentivo. Dust de arredondamento vai para toApp, preservando burned + toTreasury + toApp == amount sempre. LEGADO pos-remodel 2026-07-08.

nodes.label: Procedimento de deploy mainnet (F0-F4)
nodes.rationale: 4 fases com gates obrigatorios: F0 pre-deploy (auditoria externa, multisig 4-de-7, 14d em Sepolia, monitoramento), F1 deploy Ignition (sub-fases A-D, Timelock renuncia DEFAULT_ADMIN por ultimo), F2 bootstrap (mint minimo 12k GOV, primeira proposta = acceptOwnership), F3 distribuicao por buckets em propostas separadas, F4 handoff. Checklist L2: votingDelay/votingPeriod em blocos colapsam em chains com block time < 12s. Deploy do trilho remodel (PSM/FeeRouterV2/ProjectFunding via scripts/deploy-remodel.ts) ainda precisa ser incorporado; bloqueadores: auditoria externa + parecer juridico do rev-share.

nodes.label: Dao.ts (modulo Ignition)
nodes.rationale: Flags opcionais de build-time (default false): DEPLOY_TEAM_VESTING, DEPLOY_USER_SUBSIDY, DEPLOY_CLP_PHASE1 (gauge + distributorV2), DEPLOY_CLP_ORACLE. O modulo nao concede roles ao CLP nem chama Treasury.setPriceOracle — wiring pos-deploy e ato de governanca. Placeholder ZeroAddress do TeamVesting reverte de proposito para evitar deploy silencioso com placeholder.

nodes.label: Modelo de seguranca
nodes.rationale: Consolida invariantes, superficies de ataque e mitigacoes dos 15 contratos de producao. Decisoes conscientes: sem rescueTokens (seria backdoor governance-accessivel), sem proxies/upgrade (substituicao = deploy novo + migracao de roles), sem pause nos contratos economicos core. Threat model gradua atacantes por GOV detido; captura >50% mitigada residualmente pelo delay de 2 dias do Timelock. Slither 0.11.5 zero high/medium; 858 testes.

nodes.label: Invariantes do protocolo (I1-I9)
nodes.rationale: I1 cap GOV 100M; I2 burn no consumo (legado); I3 cap por rodada; I4 governance-only exit; I5 anti-flashloan; I6 lock minimo 14d; I7 projetos via governanca; I8 segregacao on-chain de saldos reservados (Treasury polRefillBucket+pendingGaugeRewards, Gauge totalVestingLocked); I9 supermaioria 75% para removePOL. Invariantes do trilho antigo marcadas legado pos-remodel; trilho vigente tem I-PSM1 (lastro integral), teto de fee 500 bps, conservacao toApp+fee+revShare == amount, all-or-nothing.

nodes.label: FAQ
nodes.rationale: Racional economico do remodel: fee de 2,5% vs bypass dominante do modelo antigo (~80% de taxa efetiva era equilibrio de Nash no colapso, parecer audit/economist/2026-07-08-feerouter-bypass.md). CREDIT nao valoriza por desenho (1:1 USDC via PSM); GOV captura valorizacao via buyback continuo (40% da fee = 1% do GMV). Apps usam o FeeRouterV2 porque so receita roteada gera rev-share verificavel e acesso a captacao no ProjectFunding.

nodes.label: Inspiracoes arquiteturais (Uniswap/Aave/Compound/MakerDAO/Optimism/Curve)
nodes.rationale: Padroes adotados: dual-token economy (Aave/Compound/PoolTogether), directed staking inspirado em veCRV+gauges da Curve adaptado para 1 stake = 1 projeto, burn-to-mint, permissionless finalize (pull-based como Aave/Compound rewards), timelock com delay como mitigacao de captura.

nodes.label: Templates de propostas do Governor
nodes.rationale: Scripts sao o 'gerador de calldata' da DAO: editam JSON, imprimem proposalId/calldatas/descriptionHash e abrem a proposta. Nao executam vote->queue->execute — em producao o ciclo passa por UIs de governanca (Tally, Snapshot, Etherscan).

nodes.label: propose-team-vesting.ts
nodes.rationale: TeamVesting e deploy + proposta separados porque o Timelock nao deploya contratos atomicamente — so invoca enderecos conhecidos. Alternativa VestingFactory rejeitada: (a) adiciona 1 contrato a superficie auditada para salvar 1 tx off-chain; (b) a separacao torna o review trivial (sabe-se exatamente quanto GOV e mintado e para qual endereco concreto). Instancia orfa (proposta reprovada) e inofensiva — sem GOV, sem uso.
